categories.title: Getting Started
categories.summary: Set up a profile and save your first password.

categories.title: Security Tips
categories.summary: Safer sign-in, device access, clipboard use, and irreversible actions.

categories.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
categories.summary: Find safe next steps for sign-in, device, transfer, and data problems.

topics.title: Start using Password Manager Local
topics.summary: Choose whether to create a profile or bring an existing one to this device.

sections.title: Choose the right starting point
sections.body: On the sign-in screen, choose Create a new account if this is your first profile. If your profile already exists on another device, choose Bring an existing profile from another device instead.

sections.title: Save your first password
sections.body: After signing in, open Passwords and choose Add a new password. Give the entry a name, enter the password value, and save it.

sections.title: Connect another device when needed
sections.body: You can use a local profile on one device. To use the same profile on another device, follow the two-device enrollment guide while both devices are on the same local network.

sections.title: Help is always available
sections.body: Open Settings → Help & Guide even before signing in. Reading this guide does not create a profile or change your passwords.

topics.title: Create a local account
topics.summary: Create a new profile on this device; use device enrollment for a profile you already have.

sections.title: Enter your profile details
sections.body: From Sign in, choose Create a new account. Enter a username, email address, first name, and last name. Follow the validation messages beside each field.

sections.title: Choose and confirm a master password
sections.body: Enter the password that will unlock this profile, then repeat it. The password-strength information button explains how to choose a stronger password.

sections.title: Review Remember me, then create the account
sections.body: Enable Remember me only on a device you trust. Choose Create account and wait for the result. If the app says the account was created but could not be opened, return to Sign in with these credentials instead of registering again.

sections.title: A matching username does not connect devices
sections.body: Creating another account is not a way to retrieve an existing vault. Bring the existing profile from a device where it is already available. There is no email-based password-reset flow in this app.

topics.title: Sign in to a profile
topics.summary: Use the username and master password of a profile available on this device.

sections.title: Enter your credentials
sections.body: Enter the profile username and master password, then choose Sign in. This is the profile password, not a password entry stored inside the vault.

sections.title: Decide whether to remember this profile
sections.body: Remember me lets the app restore this profile on this device. You can also change it for the active profile using the account controls after signing in. Use it only if you trust the device and its screen lock.

sections.title: Read the result before retrying
sections.body: Check the selected username, keyboard layout, and password. If you changed the master password on another device, use the new credentials. If the profile has never been on this device, enroll it first.

sections.title: Do not reset or delete data to fix a failed sign-in
sections.body: A failed sign-in does not prove that the vault should be deleted. A database reset deletes local profiles and data. There is no forgotten-password reset option; keep access to any device that still has the profile.

topics.title: Switch between profiles
topics.summary: Select another signed-in profile without copying data between accounts.

sections.title: Open the profile selector
sections.body: Use Change profile in the account controls. The selector shows available signed-in profiles. At startup, you may also be asked to choose among remembered profiles.

sections.title: Choose the profile you want to use
sections.body: Select its row and check the account name after switching. If it is not listed, use Sign in to another account. An expired session may require signing in again.

sections.title: Each profile has its own vault
sections.body: Switching changes the active profile. It does not merge vaults, transfer passwords, or add another device. To copy selected items to a different profile, use the between-profile export flow.

topics.title: Sign in to another account
topics.summary: Add another local profile to the signed-in list on this device.

sections.title: Start from Change profile
sections.body: Open the profile selector and choose Sign in to another account. Enter the other profile’s username and master password.

sections.title: Bring the profile here if necessary
sections.body: If the other profile exists only on another device, use Bring an existing profile from another device on the sign-in screen. Creating a new account would create a separate vault.

sections.title: Choose the active account deliberately
sections.body: After signing in, use Change profile to choose which vault to work with. Check the active account before adding, moving, or deleting items.

topics.title: Add and manage passwords
topics.summary: Create, find, edit, reveal, and delete entries in the active profile.

sections.title: Add an entry
sections.body: Open Passwords and choose Add a new password. Enter a name and the password value. Add a description, tags, or a color if useful, then choose Save. The editor can also generate a password.

sections.title: Find and edit an entry
sections.body: Use the search field, search-field choices, and sort order to find an entry. Open its details or choose Edit, change the values, and save. Manage tags and custom colors from the editor when needed.

sections.title: Reveal or copy only when needed
sections.body: Use the reveal or copy action for the selected entry. Copy puts the password on the device clipboard; other applications may be able to read clipboard contents. Avoid revealing secrets while sharing your screen.

sections.title: Review deletion before confirming
sections.body: Deleting an entry has no undo action in the app and can synchronize to the profile’s other devices. Check the selected entries and the active profile before confirming.

topics.title: Bring your profile to a new device
topics.summary: The new device shows a code. The already signed-in device reads it and sends the profile.

sections.title: Prepare both devices
sections.body: Install and open the app on both devices. Connect them to the same local network. Keep the existing profile signed in on the device that already has it.

sections.title: On the new device: show a connection code
sections.body: From Sign in, choose Bring an existing profile from another device, read the introduction, then choose Show connection code. Keep the QR/code screen open.

sections.title: On the existing device: choose Add device
sections.body: Open Devices → Add device. Scan the new device’s QR code, choose a QR image, or enter its connection code. This is where you approve sending this profile to the new device.

sections.title: Wait for success, then sign in on the new device
sections.body: After the profile is copied successfully, choose OK on the new device and sign in with the existing username and master password. A connection code does not replace your master password.

sections.title: Use only a code from the device you intend to add
sections.body: The code is temporary. If it expires or enrollment fails, read the displayed result before starting a new attempt. Keep codes and QR images private.

topics.title: Add a device from your signed-in profile
topics.summary: Read the connection code displayed by the new device.

sections.title: Show the code on the new device
sections.body: On the new device, open the existing-profile transfer option from Sign in and show a connection code. Both devices must remain on the same local network.

sections.title: Open Add device on the existing device
sections.body: Sign in to the profile you want to send. Open Devices → Add device. If the app says synchronization is disabled for this profile on this device, enable it in the current device’s details first.

sections.title: Android: scan with the camera
sections.body: Choose Scan QR code and grant camera permission if requested. Point the camera at the QR code on the new device. You can also choose Upload QR image or enter the code manually.

sections.title: Windows: choose an image or type the code
sections.body: Use Upload QR image to select a readable QR picture, or enter the connection code and choose Add device. Camera scanning is not offered by the current Windows app. Approve the app’s Windows Firewall setup if prompted.

sections.title: Check the result on both devices
sections.body: Scanning or choosing a valid QR image starts the add-device attempt. For a typed code, choose Add device. Wait for completion and check that the intended profile is available on the new device.

topics.title: Understand synchronization
topics.summary: Connected devices exchange updates for the same profile when they can communicate.

sections.title: One profile across enrolled devices
sections.body: Enrollment connects a device to an existing profile. Changes can then reach the profile’s other connected devices. Separately created accounts do not synchronize just because they use similar names.

sections.title: Review device-specific sync controls
sections.body: In Devices, open the current device’s details to check this profile’s local synchronization setting. Other devices also have individual synchronization controls. Read confirmation messages before changing them.

sections.title: Choose whether to allow background operation
sections.body: Settings → Background operation controls background synchronization and automatic startup. It is separate from the profile’s device synchronization switches. For an initial connection check, keep both app interfaces open.

sections.title: Offline devices may have older data
sections.body: An offline device cannot immediately receive new passwords, deletions, or device changes. Reconnect and check the displayed last-successful-sync information before assuming that another device has the latest state.

topics.title: Disconnect a device
topics.summary: Remove another device from the active profile after reviewing possible unsynchronized changes.

sections.title: Check for changes you still need
sections.body: The removed device may contain changes that have never reached this device. If it is safe and possible, let the devices synchronize before removal. Disconnecting cannot retrieve unseen changes from an offline device.

sections.title: Select the correct remote device
sections.body: Open Devices, select the other device, and choose Disconnect device. This flow removes another device; it is not the sign-out action for the current device.

sections.title: Read the warning and confirm with your password
sections.body: Check the device name, read the warning, and enter the active profile’s master password. Confirm only when you intend to remove that device’s membership in this profile.

sections.title: Removal reaches other devices through communication
sections.body: The app records the removal and sends it to peers. The removed device’s profile is removed when that device receives and applies the removal. An offline or lost device cannot be wiped immediately by this action; do not continue editing the profile there.

topics.title: Delete an account
topics.summary: Delete the active profile and propagate its deletion to connected devices.

sections.title: Account deletion is irreversible and affects this profile
sections.body: This is not sign-out or removal of just one device. It deletes the profile’s local stored data and records an account-deletion instruction for its other devices. Other independent profiles are not selected for deletion.

sections.title: Keep anything you need before deleting
sections.body: Check the active profile and any data you need to retain. If appropriate, copy selected items to another signed-in profile and verify the copies first. That copy is not a full backup of the account.

sections.title: Open Delete account and review the confirmation
sections.body: In Profile, choose Delete account. Read the warning, enter this profile’s master password, and confirm only if you want to delete the account. The app clears its local sessions after deletion.

sections.title: Other devices must receive the deletion
sections.body: An offline device can retain its old copy until it reconnects and accepts the deletion. Do not treat deletion as an immediate remote wipe. The app retains verification records needed to prevent the deleted account from being restored by old synchronized data.

topics.title: Copy or move items to another profile
topics.summary: Export here means transferring selected items between signed-in profiles on this device.

sections.title: Sign in to both profiles
sections.body: Use Change profile → Sign in to another account if needed. Return to the source profile. The destination must be a different, currently signed-in profile on this device.

sections.title: Select items and choose Export
sections.body: Select the passwords, tags, or custom colors in the appropriate list, choose Export, then select the destination account. This flow does not create a CSV or other external password file.

sections.title: Choose copy or move deliberately
sections.body: With Delete originals after export off, the app copies the selected items. With it on, the app first writes them to the destination and then removes the originals from the source. Review the target and confirm Copy or Move.

sections.title: After an error, inspect both profiles before retrying
sections.body: A destination write can succeed even if source cleanup or the final response fails. Both profiles may contain the items. Check the destination and source before repeating a move or manually deleting anything.

topics.title: Protect your master password
topics.summary: Your master password unlocks the profile; keep it distinct from passwords stored in the vault.

sections.title: Choose a long, unique password
sections.body: Choose a long, unique master password, such as a passphrase made from several randomly chosen unrelated words. Avoid quotes, personal details, predictable substitutions, and reuse from other accounts. The strength indicator is an estimate, not proof that a password is safe or has never leaked.

sections.title: There is no forgotten-password reset flow
sections.body: The app has no email reset or central service that can send your master password. Remember me is not a replacement for knowing it. Keep a safe way to remember the password outside this vault.

sections.title: Changing the password affects other devices
sections.body: Use Profile → Change master password when you know the current password. Other devices may sign the profile out after receiving the change; sign in with the new credentials. Do not delete the profile to perform a password change.

topics.title: Handle connection codes safely
topics.summary: Treat the temporary code and its QR image as private connection information.

sections.title: The new device displays the code
sections.body: Read the code only from the device you intend to add. On the trusted signed-in device, confirm that the active profile is the one you want to transfer before scanning or entering the code.

sections.title: Do not publish codes or QR images
sections.body: Do not include the code, QR image, or master password in a support message, public screenshot, or screen share. A QR image contains the same connection information as the code.

sections.title: Use the current code
sections.body: Keep the code screen open while connecting. If the app says the code has expired, start a new attempt on the new device and use the newly displayed code. Do not keep retrying an old screenshot.

sections.title: If the code was shared or scanned from the wrong device
sections.body: Cancel the exposed attempt on the new device and generate a new code only when ready. If a profile may already have been sent, inspect Devices from a trusted device and disconnect any unintended device. Replacing a code does not undo a completed transfer.

topics.title: Understand a blocked device
topics.summary: Read the reason before deciding whether a device should be unblocked.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: Device details shows Blocked, a block time or reason, or invalid sync attempts. Offline means unreachable; blocked means communication is restricted. Neither state says that the remote vault has been erased.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: Invalid or unverifiable synchronization attempts can trigger protection. The displayed reason is the starting point; a block alone does not prove an attack or ordinary network failure. Do not dismiss repeated verification failures.

sections.title: Confirm the device and review diagnostics
sections.body: Check that you recognize the device, then read its reason, time, attempt count, and last successful sync. On a working profile, use Self diagnostics and automatic safe repair where offered and read the result. For an unknown or lost device, use the lost-device guidance.

sections.title: Unblock only after resolving the concern
sections.body: Use Unblock device only when you understand the issue and still trust the device. Unblocking clears a restriction; it does not repair damaged data, restore a deleted profile, or guarantee successful sync. If the block returns, stop retrying and preserve the diagnostic details.

topics.title: Check device connection and sync problems
topics.summary: Start with the displayed status, local network, and synchronization switches.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: A device is offline, synchronization is disabled, or recent items do not appear on another device. A last-successful-sync time shows a past success, not proof that every later edit has arrived.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: The devices may not be reachable on the local network, sync may be disabled for this profile or peer, background operation may be restricted, or a protective block may prevent exchange. Internet access alone does not prove a local connection.

sections.title: Compare the profile and device settings
sections.body: Check the intended profile on both devices. Keep both apps open on the same trusted network, review synchronization switches and blocked status, then compare a known recent entry and the displayed sync time. Follow the enrollment network guide for firewall or isolation problems.

sections.title: Preserve both copies while investigating
sections.body: Do not delete profiles, reset a database, or manually copy database files over another installation to force synchronization. A device may hold edits not present elsewhere. If verification fails or a device is blocked, read the relevant safety topic before changing trust settings.

topics.title: Stay signed in safely
topics.summary: Remember me is convenient, but makes access to your device more important.

sections.title: An unlocked device can open your vault
sections.body: Remember me lets the app restore this profile without asking for your master password. Someone who can use your unlocked device may be able to open the vault. Closing the window or restarting the app does not cancel this choice.

sections.title: Use it only on a device you control
sections.body: Leave it off on shared, borrowed, public, or untrusted devices. On your own device, use a strong screen lock, a short automatic lock delay, and a separate operating-system account. Lock the device whenever you step away.

sections.title: Turn it off before signing out
sections.body: In the account menu, turn Remember Me off for the active profile and check that the change succeeds. Then sign out. Signing out alone ends that session but does not erase the saved Remember me choice. Review each remembered profile separately.

sections.title: It is not password recovery or immediate locking
sections.body: Turning the option off does not close an already open session. Keep your master password available securely outside this vault; remembered access may stop working after device changes or data problems. Switching profiles also leaves other signed-in profiles available.

topics.title: Plan for loss of access
topics.summary: Prepare before a device fails or your only copy is lost.

sections.title: Keep a separate way to remember the master password
sections.body: Keep a securely stored offline record, for example in a locked place only you can access. Do not keep the only copy inside the vault it unlocks, or in an unprotected note, photo, email, or chat.

sections.title: Check another trusted enrolled device before replacing one
sections.body: If possible, enroll another device you control. Before retiring the old device, confirm that you can sign in on the replacement and that the entries you need are present. Keep the working device until you have verified the result.

sections.title: Synchronization is not an independent backup
sections.body: Edits, deletions, and account deletion can spread to other devices. This app has no complete backup-and-restore workflow in its UI. Copying selected items to another profile is not a complete account backup, and a copied database file alone may be unusable without device-protected keys.

sections.title: Preserve your last working copy
sections.body: Do not uninstall, clear app data, reset the database, or delete the profile as a recovery experiment. There is no central vault copy or email reset. Recovery from another device depends on healthy available data and is not guaranteed.

topics.title: A device is lost or no longer trusted
topics.summary: Remove its access and protect any passwords it may already hold.

sections.title: Use a trusted remaining device
sections.body: Open the affected profile, go to Devices, identify the lost device, and choose Disconnect device. Check the name carefully and confirm with the master password. Do not wait to retrieve unseen changes from a device you no longer trust.

sections.title: Disconnection cannot recall an offline copy
sections.body: Removal must reach a device before it can apply it. Disconnection is not an immediate remote wipe, and neither a master-password change nor account deletion can erase secrets someone has already read or copied.

sections.title: Change exposed service passwords from a safe device
sections.body: Prioritize email, financial, and other important accounts. Use each service’s own security settings to change its password and revoke unfamiliar sessions. If the master password may be known, change it too. Enable MFA on services that offer it.

sections.title: Use the device platform’s protection too
sections.body: If previously configured, use the operating system’s lost-device lock or erase service. Do this from a trusted account and device. Do not share enrollment codes or passwords with anyone claiming they need them to locate your device.

topics.title: Pause before deleting an account
topics.summary: Check the scope and preserve what you need before an irreversible action.

sections.title: Choose the action that matches your intention
sections.body: Sign out ends a session. Disconnect removes another device from this profile. Delete account removes the local profile and sends an account-deletion instruction to its other devices. Database reset erases all local profiles. These actions have different consequences.

sections.title: Verify the active profile and any copies first
sections.body: Check the account name. If you need selected items elsewhere, copy them to the intended profile and open that profile to verify them before deleting anything. Do not count an unverified transfer as a backup.

sections.title: There is no undo or immediate remote wipe
sections.body: An offline device may retain its copy until it receives and applies the deletion. A second synced device is not a way to undo account deletion. Deleting this vault also does not delete your accounts at websites whose passwords you stored here.

topics.title: Copy or move: check both profiles
topics.summary: A transfer gives the destination profile its own copy of the selected data.

sections.title: Read the destination account name
sections.body: Check the source profile, destination profile, and selection before confirming. Only copy secrets into a profile whose users and enrolled devices you trust. Its copy can synchronize to that profile’s devices.

sections.title: Delete originals changes a copy into a move
sections.body: With Delete originals after export off, the source stays. With it on, the app writes the destination first, then deletes the source items. Those deletions can synchronize. A move is not a backup or a change to the password at the actual website.

sections.title: Check both sides after an uncertain result
sections.body: If an error follows confirmation, inspect the destination and source before retrying or deleting anything manually. A completed destination write may coexist with originals. Copies in separate profiles do not stay linked; future edits in one do not update the other.

topics.title: Copy passwords with care
topics.summary: Clipboard convenience can leave a secret outside the vault.

sections.title: Check the destination before pasting
sections.body: Open the intended site or app and focus its password field first. Paste once, then check that you did not put the password in a chat, search field, username field, or shared document. Do not copy secrets on an untrusted device.

sections.title: The clipboard is outside the vault
sections.body: Clipboard managers, keyboards, history, or clipboard synchronization may retain or share copied text. The app does not provide a timed clipboard-clearing guarantee. Copying harmless text afterwards replaces the current clipboard, but does not erase saved history or copies already sent elsewhere.

sections.title: Windows: review clipboard history and synchronization
sections.body: In Windows Settings → System → Clipboard, review history and cross-device synchronization. If a password appears in Win+V history, delete that item. Clear all does not remove pinned items; remove those individually too. Avoid pinning passwords.

sections.title: Android: review your keyboard’s clipboard
sections.body: If your keyboard or clipboard app has saved or pinned entries, remove the password there too. Names and retention behavior vary by device and keyboard. Do not rely on an automatic expiry to remove every copy.

topics.title: Reveal secrets only when needed
topics.summary: Screen sharing, screenshots, and nearby viewers can expose visible information.

sections.title: Pause sharing before opening sensitive screens
sections.body: Check screen recording, remote support, mirroring, and nearby viewers before revealing a password or showing an enrollment code. Even masked-password screens can expose account names, descriptions, or other identifying details.

sections.title: Hide the value again and lock the device
sections.body: After checking a password, use Hide and leave the sensitive screen. Lock the device before handing it over or stepping away. A hidden value is still accessible to someone who can use your signed-in profile.

sections.title: Hiding does not erase an earlier capture
sections.body: Screenshots and recordings may be saved or synchronized by other apps. Never send a real password or live QR/code as an example. If a password was exposed, change it at the affected service; deleting the screenshot cannot recall copies.

topics.title: Protect the device as well as the vault
topics.summary: Encrypted storage does not make an unlocked or compromised device safe.

sections.title: Use a strong device lock
sections.body: Set a strong device PIN or password and automatic screen locking. Keep operating-system accounts separate on a shared computer. Windows+L locks Windows quickly. Avoid using your vault on devices controlled by someone you do not trust.

sections.title: Install trusted updates
sections.body: Keep the operating system, app, browser, and keyboard updated through trusted sources. Be cautious with remote-control tools, unknown extensions, and apps requesting broad accessibility or screen-capture access. Such access may expose what you type or view.

sections.title: Encryption has limits while you use the app
sections.body: The app uses encrypted local storage, but an open profile can display and copy secrets. Encryption does not protect a password after it reaches a screenshot, clipboard, malicious app, or another person. Offline use does not remove these risks.

sections.title: Closing the interface is not a security lock
sections.body: Background synchronization can continue when enabled, and Remember me can restore access. Use the device lock and review remembered profiles rather than assuming that closing a window, switching profiles, or disabling synchronization signs you out.

topics.title: Practical habits for everyday passwords
topics.summary: Use unique credentials and check where you enter them.

sections.title: Generate a different long password for each service
sections.body: Use the password generator in the editor, within the service’s allowed length and character rules. Avoid predictable variations of one password. Your master password should be unique too; never use it as a website password.

sections.title: Editing an entry does not change the website password
sections.body: Change the password in the actual service’s account settings, update the vault entry, and verify that the new credential works before discarding the old one. If a password was reused or exposed, change it at every affected service from a trusted device.

sections.title: Open the known service yourself
sections.body: Use a trusted bookmark or type the known address before pasting a password. Check the address, not just the logo. Do not enter passwords or enrollment codes through urgent links in messages, and never approve an unexpected sign-in request.

sections.title: Enable extra protection at the services you use
sections.body: Where offered, enable multifactor authentication (MFA) in the service itself, especially for email and important accounts. Keep its recovery codes somewhere safe outside a single device. Storing a password here does not enable MFA at that service.

topics.title: Report a problem without sharing secrets
topics.summary: Share the symptom and app version, then review every attachment.

sections.title: Start with non-sensitive facts
sections.body: Note the app version from Settings → About, platform, action, and visible error or status. Explain whether one or both devices are affected. Replace personal names and account details with neutral labels in your description.

sections.title: Logs and screenshots are not automatically safe to share
sections.body: Review technical details and attachments for passwords, notes, QR images, enrollment codes, account identifiers, paths, and network addresses. Never send database files or protected keys as a routine support attachment. Do not assume a full log is anonymous.

sections.title: Use a harmless example when possible
sections.body: Describe steps using made-up entries or a separate test profile if it is safe to reproduce. A request for your master password or a live connection code is not needed to read an error message. Stop if someone asks you to reveal them.

topics.title: Cannot sign in or restore a remembered profile
topics.summary: Check credentials and preserve any device that still has access.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: The app reports incorrect credentials, an expired or invalid session, or that remembered sessions could not be restored. A local-data verification message is a different problem and may occur even when your password is unchanged.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: The username, keyboard layout, or password may differ from what you intended. The profile may not exist on this device yet, a master password may have changed, or the device may no longer be able to restore saved access.

sections.title: Try a deliberate manual sign-in
sections.body: Check the username and keyboard layout. Use the current master password, not a vault entry’s password. For an expired session or failed remembered restore, sign in manually. For local-data verification failure, signing in may attempt authenticated recovery; success is not guaranteed.

sections.title: If the profile has never been on this device
sections.body: Use Bring an existing profile from another device with a trusted device that has it. Registering the same name creates no connection to the old vault. If another session is already available, check Change profile first.

sections.title: No email reset or guaranteed recovery
sections.body: If you forgot the master password, preserve any working session and read the recovery advice. Do not delete, reset, or reinstall to test a fix. If the error persists, record the safe details rather than repeatedly changing or erasing data.

topics.title: The new device cannot be found or connected
topics.summary: Separate local-network problems from code and profile-data errors.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: The message says the new device was not found, could not be connected, no usable local network was found, or the local enrollment service could not start. Finding device details does not always mean the transfer connection can reach it.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: Guest Wi-Fi, client isolation, separate Wi-Fi and wired segments, firewall rules, or a closed code screen can prevent contact. Devices with internet access can still be unable to reach each other locally.

sections.title: Keep both apps open on a trusted local network
sections.body: Connect both devices to the same trusted local network and keep the new device’s current code screen open. Check Wi-Fi or Ethernet on each. If a local service could not start, reconnect to that network and start a fresh attempt.

sections.title: Windows: check the app’s local-network permission
sections.body: Review the app’s firewall configuration prompt on your trusted network. If needed, ask the network administrator about local-subnet access and guest/client isolation. Do not disable the firewall, open router ports to the internet, or bypass network policy.

sections.title: Follow the message for a different failure
sections.body: If synchronization is disabled, enable it for the intended profile on the current device. For an invalid or expired code, use code help. For rejection, incompatible data, or a partial result, inspect both devices and use the profile-transfer error topic.

topics.title: A connection code is invalid or expired
topics.summary: Use the current code from the new device, not an old image.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: The app reports an invalid, incomplete, expired, or unverifiable code. It may also reject a code belonging to the same device where you are trying to add it.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: A character may be missing, the QR image may be old, or the temporary attempt may have ended. The new device displays the code; the already signed-in device reads it. Reversing these roles will not connect the profile.

sections.title: Start a new attempt on the intended new device
sections.body: Show a fresh connection code there and keep the screen open. Read that code from Add device on your trusted signed-in device. For manual entry, include the whole code; the slash marks zero, not the letter O. Never post a code for someone else to check.

topics.title: Profile transfer was rejected or only partly completed
topics.summary: Keep both copies while you check the result and the specific error.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: The new device rejects the transfer, the profile cannot be imported, its data is too large, an identity conflicts, or the app reports a partially completed operation. An error after starting a transfer does not prove that nothing changed.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: The app may be protecting account consistency, detecting incompatible data, enforcing a size limit, or finding an existing device identity. These are not all fixed by generating codes repeatedly.

sections.title: Inspect both devices before another attempt
sections.body: Check whether the intended profile is present on the new device and review Devices on the existing one. Follow any explicit restart instruction first. For an ordinary rejection with no partial-result warning, generate a fresh code and retry once; stop if it repeats.

sections.title: Match the action to the error
sections.body: For incompatible versions, check trusted app updates on both devices. For invalid profile data, review self diagnostics on the working profile. For size limits or identity conflicts, preserve the existing data and report safe details; do not delete entries or edit identity files just to force enrollment.

sections.title: Do not reset the only working copy
sections.body: Keep the source profile and any healthy enrolled device. Do not remove device records, clear app data, or reset a database to make a partial-result message disappear. If the result remains uncertain, get the error reviewed before further changes.

topics.title: Cannot scan or read a QR image
topics.summary: Try a clearer current code or manual entry without weakening device security.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: The camera will not start, the QR image cannot be read, or no usable code is returned. A readable image can still contain an expired code; that requires a new attempt rather than a better photo.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: Permission may be denied, the code may be cropped, or glare and blur may prevent reading. An unrelated QR code is not an enrollment code. The current Windows app does not offer camera scanning.

sections.title: Use the whole current code
sections.body: Keep the new device’s code screen open. Show the full QR with its border, avoid glare, and use a sharp image. Alternatively, enter the complete code manually on the existing device. Do not upload it to an online QR-decoding service.

sections.title: Android: review camera permission
sections.body: If you want camera scanning, review this app’s camera permission in Android settings. If you prefer not to grant it, use image selection or manual entry. Only the scanning option needs the camera.

topics.title: Data verification or self diagnostics needs attention
topics.summary: Let the app check safe repairs without assuming every problem is recoverable.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: The app reports that data could not be verified, or self diagnostics reports healthy data, a safe local repair, or an issue that cannot be repaired automatically. Some findings concern device links or account history rather than a forgotten password.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: The app refuses to treat inconsistent or unverifiable data as trustworthy. Safe automatic repair is limited to supported cases. A healthy result is not a complete security audit and does not prove that another device has every recent edit.

sections.title: Read the exact diagnostic result
sections.body: Where available in device details, run Self diagnostics and automatic safe repair, then read the outcome. For a sign-in verification warning, follow the sign-in advice. Keep any healthy device and record the non-sensitive finding and version if attention is still required.

sections.title: Do not bypass verification
sections.body: Do not edit database files, delete account history, repeatedly unblock a device, or reset the database to suppress the warning. Recovery can depend on a healthy peer and available evidence; neither diagnostics nor remembered access guarantees recovery.

topics.title: Updates stop when the app is closed
topics.summary: Background operation and profile-specific synchronization are separate settings.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: Updates arrive only while both interfaces are open, or Settings shows background operation as unavailable, degraded, or unable to configure startup or save the setting.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: Background operation may be disabled, the operating system may restrict it, or a saved preference may not match the running state. A device can also be offline, blocked, or have synchronization disabled for this profile.

sections.title: Check foreground sync first, then the displayed background state
sections.body: Keep both apps open on the same trusted local network and review device status. Then open Settings → Background operation, review the actual state and error, and retry after resolving the reported problem. Do not assume an enabled preference proves successful synchronization.

sections.title: Android: review app-specific system restrictions
sections.body: Check battery and background restrictions for this app if synchronization stops while it is not visible. Device settings vary. After a restart, unlock the device before expecting protected local data to be available. Review permissions narrowly rather than disabling system protections globally.

sections.title: Windows: follow the reported startup or save failure
sections.body: Automatic startup is configured for the current Windows user. If configuration or persistence fails, read the error and check normal access for that user. If the state cannot be read, retry when the app is ready. Do not run the app permanently as administrator as a workaround.

topics.title: Between-profile export failed or has no destination
topics.summary: Check signed-in profiles and inspect both sides after confirmation.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: No destination account is listed, an export action is disabled, or the operation reports an error. Duplicate names, profile limits, or an expired session may also prevent an operation.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: The destination must be another currently signed-in profile on this device. An account on another device alone is not a destination. An error after confirmation may occur after items were already written to the destination.

sections.title: Check the destination, then the source
sections.body: For no destination, sign in to another account and return to the source. For an error after confirmation, inspect the actual entries in both profiles before retrying. Follow specific name or limit messages without deleting unrelated data to make room.

sections.title: Do not assume a failed move left the source untouched
sections.body: A destination write can succeed before source cleanup or a final response fails. Keep any surviving copies until verified. A new attempt can create conflicts or additional copies. This export transfers items between profiles; it is not an external file backup.

topics.title: The database cannot be opened or a reset is offered
topics.summary: Stop before erasing local data, especially if this is your only copy.

sections.title: What you see
sections.body: The app reports an unsupported database version, a missing or damaged configuration header, a failed reset, or a backend startup failure. The database-version screen may offer Reset database and a second permanent-erasure confirmation.

sections.title: Why it can happen
sections.body: An incompatible app version, damaged local configuration, or startup/access problem can prevent opening the store. This is not evidence that your master password should be changed. Recreating a local store is different from recovering its contents.

sections.title: Preserve the data and check trusted version information
sections.body: If you need the local data, decline the reset and close the app. Check whether you started an older app version and whether a trusted compatible update is available. Preserve any other working device. Report the version and safe error details if the problem remains.

sections.title: Reset deletes every local profile
sections.body: Reset permanently removes the local database, its protected key, profiles, passwords, and local synchronization data. Reinstallation or clearing app data can also destroy access. Do not use these as a routine troubleshooting step; rebuilding from another device is not guaranteed.

topics.title: Frequently asked questions
topics.summary: Short answers about offline access, recovery, profiles, and deletion.

sections.title: Can I use it without internet?
sections.body: You can work with a profile already available on this device without internet access. Enrollment and synchronization need the devices to communicate on a suitable local network. Offline devices do not immediately receive other devices’ edits or deletions.

sections.title: Can an email or central server restore my password?
sections.body: No email-reset or central vault-recovery service is provided. A newly registered account with the same details does not retrieve your previous vault. Remembered access is convenient but is not a replacement for knowing your master password.

sections.title: Does signing out turn off Remember me?
sections.body: No. Turn Remember Me off for that profile in the account menu and check success before signing out if you want to stop automatic restoration. Review other signed-in profiles too; switching profiles is not signing them out.

sections.title: Is Export a file backup?
sections.body: The current Export action copies or moves selected items to another signed-in profile on this device. It does not create a CSV or full backup file. Synchronization is not an independent backup because deletions can synchronize too.

sections.title: Does changing or deleting a vault entry change my website account?
sections.body: No. A vault entry stores information. Change the actual password or close the actual account using that service’s own settings. If a password leaked, deleting its vault entry does not revoke it.

sections.title: Does disconnecting or deleting immediately erase an offline device?
sections.body: No. A remote device has to receive and apply the change. Do not rely on this as an immediate remote wipe, and do not treat a blocked status as proof that an existing copy was erased. Use the lost-device advice if access may have been exposed.
